CAD/CAM provisional blocks and crowns are superior in their flexural strength as well as vertical marginal adaptation as compared to bis-acrylic provisional blocks and crow ns.
CAD/CAM technique is superior to the traditional direct technique for the fabrication of temporary crowns in terms of vertical marginal gap.

CAD CAM provisional materials are better than the traditional bis acrylic composite based provisional materials in terms of marginal adaptation and are comparable to them in terms of flexural strength.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
CAD CAM provisional crowns have better marginal adaptation than bis acrylic composite based provisional crowns and both the materials have comparable flexure strength.

CAD/CAM provisional blocks and CAD/CAM crowns showed better results in terms of flexural strength as well as marginal adaptation when compared to the bis acrylic composite based provisional materials.
CAD CAM provisional materials can be used for temporary restorations with good results in terms of marginal fit and strength.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the CAD/CAM provisional crown material has superior marginal adaptation as compared to Protemp(tm) material.

CAD/CAM provisional blocks can be used for the fabrication of provisional crowns as the marginal adaptation of the crowns fabricated by the CAD/CAM technique was better than that of the crowns prepared with Protemp(tm)4.
